parameters.query:
SELECT
  title,
  url,
  source,
  link_label AS "linkLabel",
  score,
  category,
  summary
FROM discoveries
ORDER BY score DESC
LIMIT 15;

const articles = $("Code in JavaScript").all().map(item => item.json);

const grouped = articles.map((a, i) => `
${i + 1}. TITLE: ${a.title}

const prompt = `
You are writing a high-performing LinkedIn post for Elegant Frontend.

Use the discoveries below:

${grouped}

Write a concise LinkedIn post for frontend developers, technical founders, and engineering leaders.

STRICT RULES:

- Start with a strong hook in the first sentence
- Use short paragraphs only
- Mention at least 2 real tools, products, companies, or technologies by name from the titles above
- Mention at most 4 named products/tools
- Include exactly 3 bullet points
- You MUST format the 3 key takeaways as bullet points starting with •
- Each bullet point should be one short sentence only
- Explain why these tools or trends matter
- Focus on shifts in developer behavior, tooling, AI workflows, privacy, speed, and product simplicity
- Avoid generic phrases like "AI everywhere", "the future is bright", "things are changing", or "technology is evolving"
- Avoid vague statements with no examples
- End with a short takeaway paragraph
- End with a CTA question
- End with exactly these hashtags on the final line:
#frontend #webdev #ai
- Professional tone
- No emojis
- No markdown
- Maximum 220 words
- Return plain text only

Good example style:

Frontend teams are becoming more selective about the tools they adopt.

This week, products like Marco and Looseleaf highlighted a shift toward privacy-first workflows and faster local tooling. Developers are prioritizing tools that feel simpler, faster, and easier to integrate into existing workflows.

• Marco shows that privacy-first products are becoming more important
• Looseleaf reflects demand for more flexible developer tooling
• TailorToJob highlights how AI is being used for practical workflows instead of hype

The strongest developer tools are becoming simpler, not bigger.

Which trend do you think will matter most this year?

#frontend #webdev #ai
`;

return [{
  json: {
    prompt,
    finalDraft: $json.finalDraft,
    wasRefined: $json.wasRefined
  }
}];
